title: feat(types): derive FilterOperatorSchema from the protocol's operator set (objectui#9559)
body:
Fixes #9559
Clause-②: yes

## What this does

`FilterOperatorSchema` in `@object-ui/types/zod` was a hand-copied 14-member literal, six members behind `@objectstack/spec` (`icontains`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty`, `before`, `after`, `between`), and it refused every alias the protocol normalises. So the authoring gate (`safeValidateSchema`, `objectui check` / `objectui validate`) refused operators that the protocol's own `ViewFilterRuleSchema` and the runtime both accept.

Per the ruling on objectui#9559 (letter B, ratified): the mirror is now the spec rule's **own** `operator` member, `stripImportedDefaults(SpecViewFilterRuleSchema).shape.operator`, which the spec builds as `z.preprocess(normalizeFilterOperator, z.enum(VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS))`. So:

- all 20 canonical members of `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` are accepted;
- every row of the spec's alias table (`lessThan`, `greaterOrEqual`, `gt`, `isNull`, ...) is accepted **and normalised** to its canonical member on parse;
- everything the protocol refuses is still refused (`containsCaseInsensitive`, `exists`, `notExists` included). No local alias row was added.

The TS twin `FilterBuilderOperator` (`packages/types/src/complex.ts`) is now the spec's `ViewFilterOperator` by reference: canonical spellings only, since the spec marks its alias table a deprecated bridge that new producers must not emit.

**Route note (Zone 1 text vs. the means used).** The binding text says "import `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` ... rather than a local literal". This PR takes the spec rule's operator member instead of rebuilding `z.preprocess(normalizeFilterOperator, z.enum(VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS))` locally. The schema is identical: a pin asserts reference identity with `ViewFilterRuleSchema.shape.operator`. The reason is the objectui#8317 import-boundary census (`imported-defaults-8317.test.ts`). It requires every spec value read in a mirror to pass through `stripImportedDefaults`, which has an arm for a schema but none for a bare array or a function. The same file's `FilterFieldSchema.operators` comment records that exact constraint. So the rule schema goes through the boundary, and it is registered in that test's `IMPORTED` differential as the test instructs. No new exception category was needed.

## objectui#9306 remains open

objectui#9306 remains open. This PR carries its item 1 (the mirror is the protocol set) and the `@object-ui/types` half of its item 4 (`FilterBuilderOperator` is typed as the protocol set). Its item 2, the dropdown emitting the 20 protocol ids, **stopped on a file-surface breach and was not started**. Measured on this branch, the builder's camelCase ids are read LITERALLY by consumer translation tables outside the claim's file surface:

- `packages/fields/src/widgets/FilterConditionField.tsx`: `condToMongo` switches on `'greaterOrEqual'`, `'notEquals'`, `'isNull'`, ... and its `default` arm emits `{ [field]: cv }`. So a canonical `greater_than_or_equal` row would be stored as an **equality** in a sharing rule's criteria, with no error. `kvToCondition`, `FILTER_CONDITION_EXTRA_OPERATORS` and `TEXT_COMPARAND_OPERATORS` are keyed the same way.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/datasetFilterCondition.ts`: `OP_TO_MONGO` / `MONGO_TO_OP` / `VALUELESS_TO_MONGO` are camelCase-keyed, and an unmapped operator is dropped. So every canonical id except the six spelled identically would silently drop the row.
- `packages/plugin-view/src/config/view-config-utils.ts` `CANONICAL_TO_BUILDER` and `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` `SPEC_TO_FB` map onto camelCase ids. They are read-side and would survive through the builder's fold, but their parity pins read `FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS`.

Separately, the rulings disagree on `exists` / `notExists`. objectui#9559's ruling keeps them opt-in with their named upstream blocker. objectui#9306's amendment folds them onto `is_not_null` / `is_null` on read. The `OPT_IN_OPERATORS` record (objectui#4736) refuses that fold because `$exists` is key-presence on some drivers. Both points went back to the PM as decisions in the dev report on #9559. The containsCaseInsensitive-to-icontains spec alias card is the seat's to file, and is not filed here.

## Clause-② — exported symbols whose shape or values move (all `@object-ui/types`)

- `FilterOperatorSchema` (`@object-ui/types/zod`): a `ZodEnum` of 14 becomes the spec's `ZodPreprocess` pipe into an enum of 20. `.options` is gone; the canonical members are `FilterOperatorSchema.out.options`. The accept set widens to the 20 members plus the spec's alias table. **The parse output is normalised**, so an authored `greaterOrEqual` parses to `greater_than_or_equal`.
- `FilterBuilderOperator` (`@object-ui/types`): a 14-member local union (with `is_empty`/`is_not_empty`, without `is_null`/`is_not_null`) becomes the spec's `ViewFilterOperator` (20).
- Moved transitively by the two above: `FilterBuilderCondition.operator`, `AdvancedFilterOperator` (it unions `FilterBuilderOperator`), and the accept set and parse output of `FilterBuilderConditionSchema`, `FilterGroupSchema` and `FilterBuilderSchema`.
- **Not moved:** `FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS`, `VALUELESS_FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS` and everything else in `@object-ui/components`. No components file is in this diff.

Changeset: `.changeset/9559-filter-operator-schema-protocol-set.md`, `minor` on `@object-ui/types`. It names the visible change: the stored normalised shape of an authored camelCase operator.

## Pins

New file: `packages/types/src/__tests__/filter-operator-protocol-set-9559.test.ts`.

- (a) Reference identity with the spec rule's member. All 20 canonical members are accepted as themselves. Every alias row is accepted and normalised. The probes the protocol refuses stay refused, with `invalid_value` as the positive control that the refusal path is live. A differential against `ViewFilterRuleSchema.shape.operator` over every canonical member, every alias row, the builder's dropdown ids and the probes agrees on verdict and output, and the pin asserts that all three outcomes occurred.
- Round trip: an authored `filter-builder` node with `greaterOrEqual` / `lt` / `isNull` validates and parses to canonical spellings.
- (e) mirror side: value-less operators need no value.
- Type-level: `FilterBuilderOperator` and `z.output` of the mirror each equal `ViewFilterOperator`, and an alias is a `@ts-expect-error`.
- (d): the catalog entries PR objectui#9558 pinned still validate as authored. The two objectui#9558 refusal pins that named this key moved to their opposite in `filter-builder-mirror-6939.test.ts` (types) and in `filter-builder-operator-vocabulary-6939.test.tsx` (catalog). They are "accepted and normalised back", each with an anti-vacuity leg and a control for an invented operator that is still refused.
- (b) and (c) (the dropdown and its stored-camelCase round trip) are **NOT MEASURED**: the dropdown half was not started (see above).

## Acceptance notes

- `check:changeset-claims` flagged pending bodies that name `complex.ts` / `complex.zod.ts`, and I read the five about this operator surface. Two sentences go false inside this same release, and each got an in-release supersession note: the objectui#6939 mirror changeset's "which this mirror also refuses", and the objectui#7760 changeset's `is_null` / `is_not_null` half. Package names and bump levels are unchanged (`check-changeset-overwrite` case 2).
- `FilterFieldSchema.operators` in the same file is still a spelled-out copy of `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`. Its drift is already guarded at runtime by `mirror-groups-cd-10286.test.ts`, and deriving it (for example from `FilterOperatorSchema.out`) is outside this ruling. Noted, not changed.
- The published doc (`filter-builder.mdx`) types `operator` as `string`, which is still true. No doc change.
